summary: Localized GPU starvation in us-west reserved pool caused by quiet ephemeral fanout and prefetch shadowing
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (NimbusDocs) reported sustained p95/p99 latency increase and a drop in throughput for their dedicated reserved pool in us-west-2 between 09:30-12:45 PDT on 2026-03-10. The effect was localized to a subset of GPU hosts in the reserved cluster and coincided with many long-lived, low-throughput connections from the customer service. Impact: degraded inference performance for critical routes (chat-backend); downstream timeouts and 429s observed when fallback policy attempted burst routing.

Impact:
- Affected tenant: NimbusDocs (dedicated pool).
- Observed p99 token latency increase from ~220ms to ~1200ms for several routes.
- Throughput (tokens/s) for pinned model redwood-3b-onnx dropped ~45% on impacted hosts.
- Autoscaler did not add capacity despite higher queue depth on affected nodes.

Environment:
- Dedicated reserved cluster: us-west-2-dedicated-37
- Serving runtime: v2026.02.11, allocator v1.14.2, autoscaler v2.3.0
- Customer config: model pins, min_replicas=2, burst_capacity enabled

Steps to reproduce / observed sequence:
1) Customer reported degraded p99 and timeouts at 09:32 PDT.
2) Support pulled allocator and attach logs for hosts in reserved-37.
3) We observed many long-lived connections with tiny request volumes (keep-alive streams) originating from a cohort of customer workers (high connection fanout but low per-conn throughput).
4) Prefetcher logs show aggressive KV prefetch reservations owned by these streams; batcher slots on the same GPUs became unavailable for larger batches.
5) Autoscaler telemetry showed low global CPU and aggregated GPU utilization (below scaling thresholds) so it did not scale up; however per-host queue depth and attach latency were elevated.

Observed logs/metrics (high level):
- allocator.attach_latency.p95 (impacted hosts): 430ms -> 1.6s
- batcher.available_slots (impacted hosts): 18 -> 2
- kv_prefetch.reservations: spike of small reservations tied to ~1.8k persistent connections
- scheduler.detach_rate: elevated but not enough global signal for autoscaler

Additional notes:
Customer indicated they had a recent client-side SDK rollout that moved to long-lived multiplexed connections to reduce connection overhead. This coincided with incident window.

2026-03-10 10:28 - SRE (Diego): Pulled allocator logs for reserved-37. Noted per-host queue depth mismatch vs cluster-level utilization. Opened hypothesis: quiet, long-lived connections are hoarding prefetch/batcher slots leading to localized starvation.

2026-03-10 11:12 - Eng (Priya): Reproduced small-reservation pattern in staging by simulating many tiny, long-lived streams. Saw batcher slot fragmentation and decreased batch assembly efficiency. Logging PR proposed to surface per-stream reservation size into telemetry.

2026-03-12 14:02 - SRE (Diego): Applied temporary routing change for NimbusDocs to favor alternate hosts in the same region; observed immediate partial recovery. Continuing analysis for permanent mitigation.
2026-03-13 08:55 - Eng (Priya): Autoscaler sensitivity patch merged to PR #14456 to include per-host queue-depth signal in scale decision. Will roll to staging for 24h soak before prod rollout.
investigation_notes:
Hypotheses evaluated:
- Noisy-neighbor: confirmed. Many small long-lived streams created prefetched KV reservations and held batcher slots, starving larger batches.
- Autoscaler blind spot: autoscaler aggregates cluster signals and ignored per-host queue depth; low CPU/utilization prevented scaling.
- Network/TLS issues: ruled out — TLS handshakes normal, attach jitter correlated with host-level reservation saturation.
Evidence: allocator traces show consistent reservation owner IDs mapping to the customer's worker IPs. Staging replay of similar connection pattern reproduced slot fragmentation and p99 degradation.
Next investigative steps: collect more granular per-tenant reservation histograms and examine history to find when reservation guards changed (possible side-effect of SDK change).
workarounds: 1) Support temporarily re-routed a portion of NimbusDocs traffic to warm fallback hosts in us-east-1 which restored throughput for critical routes.
2) Customer rolled back SDK behavior to disable long-lived multiplex keepalive for the most aggressive worker pool (manual config change) — immediate improvement in slot availability.
3) Applied a per-tenant rate limiter on prefetch reservations as an emergency throttle to prevent one tenant consuming disproportionate batcher slots (hotfix rule applied to reserved-37).
resolution:
Work in progress. Short-term mitigations implemented: traffic reroute, customer-side SDK rollback, emergency prefetch throttle. Medium-term fixes planned and in progress: (a) autoscaler change to incorporate per-host queue-depth and reservation-weighted telemetry (PR #14456), (b) instrumentation change to surface per-stream reservation sizes in Console and alerts, (c) scheduler/allocator patch to enforce soft caps on prefetch reservations per-tenant.
Rollout plan: autoscaler and allocator patches to staging on 2026-03-14, 48h soak, canary to 10% prod reserved clusters on 2026-03-17, full rollout after validation. Post-incident follow-up: postmortem and permanent customer-facing mitigation guide.
